mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% over a 3-month window indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of months when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is rising (indicating monetary tightening) and the unemployment rate is simultaneously increasing (indicating labor market weakness), the combined effect signals a high probability of economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE rising) fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a decline in housing starts below 1350 thousand units signals weakening consumer confidence and reduced construction activity, which typically precedes a slowdown in corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of months when HOUST falls below 1350.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production above its 6-month moving average indicates robust manufacturing activity and economic growth, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of months when INDPRO is above its 6-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts above 1400 thousand units over the past month signals strong consumer demand for housing and a resilient economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of months when HOUST exceeds 1400.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) both increase simultaneously, it indicates a broad-based economic expansion with strong demand and supply, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST rising and INDPRO rising) fails to predict positive returns in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, when the federal funds rate is above 2.0% and rising, the cumulative effect of higher borrowing costs typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of months when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising.
